headline.title: GPT-5.6 is now the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot
headline.summary: Microsoft has integrated GPT-5.6 into its 365 Copilot, enhancing AI capabilities across applications like Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Chat. This update aims to improve efficiency and output quality for users.

articles.title: Meta enters the crowded AI coding battle with Muse Spark 1.1
articles.summary: Meta has launched Muse Spark 1.1, an AI coding tool designed to assist users with large agentic workloads, bug fixes, and extensive code migrations. This move positions Meta within the competitive landscape of AI coding solutions aimed at enterprise automation.

articles.title: Paris-based AI voice startup Gradium raises $100M seed, backed by Nvidia
articles.summary: Paris-based AI voice startup Gradium has raised $100 million in seed funding, with backing from Nvidia. The company plans to use the funds to establish an office in the Bay Area to enhance its competitive edge in the AI talent market.

articles.title: Anthropic Wants You to Pay Up for Claude Fable 5
articles.summary: Anthropic is introducing usage-based fees for subscribers of its Claude Fable 5 AI model, marking a shift in its pricing strategy. This change indicates a potential end to the era of flat-rate AI subscription services.

articles.title: GPT-5.5 Bio Bug Bounty
articles.summary: OpenAI has launched the GPT-5.5 Bio Bug Bounty program, aimed at identifying and addressing vulnerabilities in its AI models related to biological data. The initiative encourages researchers and developers to report bugs in exchange for rewards, enhancing the safety and reliability of AI applications in the biomedical field.

articles.title: GPT-5.6: Frontier intelligence that scales with your ambition
articles.summary: The article introduces GPT-5.6, highlighting its enhanced intelligence and performance efficiency, which allows for greater capability and cost-effectiveness in handling complex tasks. The new model aims to scale with user ambition, providing improved outcomes from every token processed.

articles.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-5.6 after government greenlight — and announces ‘ChatGPT Work’
articles.summary: OpenAI has officially launched GPT-5.6 following regulatory approval, initially making it available only to government-approved organizations during a limited preview. The company also announced "ChatGPT Work," a new offering aimed at enhancing productivity for users.

articles.title: The 1X Neo Robot Has Freaky Fast Fingers
articles.summary: The 1X Neo Robot features advanced tactile hands designed for home chores, enabling it to perform tasks with remarkable dexterity. This development highlights the growing integration of robotics into everyday domestic activities.

articles.title: AI 2040: Plan A
articles.summary: The AI Futures Project has released a new scenario titled "AI 2040: Plan A," which outlines recommendations for delaying the development of superintelligence until 2040, rather than the previously anticipated 2030. This scenario is intended as a guide for future AI governance rather than a prediction of actual events.

articles.title: Anthropic found a hidden space where Claude puzzles over concepts
articles.summary: Anthropic has introduced a tool called the Jacobian lens, which allows researchers to better understand the inner workings of large language models like Claude. Their findings reveal a range of insights, from ordinary to concerning, about how these models process and respond to information.

articles.title: How did the government decide OpenAI’s frontier model was safe to release?
articles.summary: The article discusses the government's evaluation process for determining the safety of OpenAI's frontier model before its release, highlighting the lack of transparency regarding the discussions between the government, Anthropic, and OpenAI. It emphasizes the uncertainty surrounding the specific dialogues that informed the decision-making process.

articles.title: Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX are bigger than the last 25 years of tech exits
articles.summary: Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX are poised to create greater financial value through their upcoming IPOs than all U.S. venture capital-backed exits combined since 2000. This trend highlights the significant impact and potential of AI companies in the tech landscape.
